title: The queen
summary: The queen moves like a rook and a bishop combined. Learn how strong she is, and how to use her to attack two things at once.

steps.title: Rook plus bishop
steps.text: The queen moves in straight lines like a rook and along diagonals like a bishop, as far as she likes. From the center she reaches 27 squares. She is the strongest piece on the board, worth about as much as a rook and a bishop together.
steps.narration: Here comes the queen, the most powerful piece in chess. She moves like a rook and a bishop rolled into one: straight lines and diagonals, as far as she wants.

steps.title: Collect the stars
steps.narration: The queen goes straight and diagonal. Grab every star in as few moves as you can.

steps.title: Patience with the queen
steps.text: Because she is so valuable, the queen has to run whenever a cheaper piece attacks her. Don't bring her out too early: in the demo, Black develops a knight with an attack on her, and White has to waste another move.
steps.narration: One warning: don't rush your queen out. Say White jumps her out to g4 on move two. [move] Black just develops a knight, and it attacks her. [move] So the queen has to run again. [move] See? Black got a piece out for free, and White wasted a move.

steps.title: Capture!
steps.narration: Lots of targets, but only one has a clear path. Find it and take it.

steps.title: Take the loose rook
steps.prompt: Black's rook on h5 is unprotected. Capture it with your queen.
steps.hint: The queen can move like a bishop. Follow the diagonal from d1.
steps.success: The diagonal from d1 to h5 was open, so the queen used her bishop powers to win a rook.
steps.narration: Black's rook on h5 has no protection. Your queen is far away on d1, but she can travel diagonally like a bishop. Find the path and grab it.

steps.title: Two attacks at once
steps.prompt: Give a check that also attacks the knight on h4, then win the knight.
steps.hint: From a4 the queen looks at e8 along a diagonal and at h4 along the fourth rank.
steps.success: Queen to a4 checked the king and attacked the knight at the same time. Black had to deal with the check, so the knight fell.
steps.narration: Because the queen moves in so many directions, she can attack two things at once. Find a check that also hits the knight. Black will be busy saving the king, and the knight is yours.

steps.title: Quick check
steps.question: Why is it usually a bad idea to bring the queen out in the first few moves?

options.text: Smaller pieces can attack her and she must keep moving, which wastes time
options.why: Each time she runs, your opponent gets to develop another piece for free.

options.text: The queen is not allowed to move before the other pieces
options.why: She may move at any time. It is just usually not a good idea early on.

options.text: The queen is weak at the start of the game
options.why: She is always the strongest piece. Her value is exactly why she gets chased.

steps.narration: Last question, and then you know the queen. Why should you be patient with her in the opening?
